title: 7 Best Semrush Alternatives for Tracking AI Visibility in 2026
summary: AI visibility isn't a future problem. It's a current operating reality that traditional SEO toolkits were never architected to measure.
body_markdown:
## Introduction


AI visibility isn't a future problem. It's a current operating reality that traditional SEO toolkits were never architected to measure. When a prospect asks ChatGPT or Perplexity for a recommendation and your brand isn't cited, that conversation leaves no footprint in Semrush, Ahrefs, or Google Search Console. The citation gap is widening.


A seismic shift in search behavior makes this urgent.[About 68% of Google searches ended without a click in early 2026](https://kime.ai/blog/best-ai-visibility-tools) . Meanwhile, ChatGPT passed 800 million weekly active users in late 2025. Discovery is moving to generative engines that extract answers rather than routing traffic. Traditional analytics miss these interactions entirely, creating a growing blind spot for any team that relies on organic acquisition.


Semrush has started bridging this gap with its AI Visibility Toolkit, bundled inside Semrush One at[$199/month](https://www.semrush.com/blog/best-ai-visibility-tools/) . But its AI tracking remains additive to a platform built for classical SEO metrics. Dedicated Generative Engine Optimization platforms track how AI systems find, judge, and cite content across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews.


This listicle evaluates the specialized alternatives that close the AI visibility gap. Each option tracks the platforms where your buyers now research, and where your competitors are already being cited.


## Key Takeaways


Here are the decisive conclusions from the full comparison.


- **Best all-around alternative:** RadarKit AI covers six LLMs, includes local tracking and AI agent monitoring, and starts at $29/month, the broadest coverage at the lowest price point.
- **Best budget entry point:** RadarKit AI at $29/month offers the most affordable path to multi-platform AI citation and competitor tracking without sacrificing coverage scope.
- **Best technical option:** Promptwatch and ZipTie, at $95/month and $69/month respectively, focus exclusively on AI crawler logs and referral traffic analysis for teams that need server-level data.
- **Semrush's missing feature:** Native, multi-platform AI visibility benchmarking is absent from the core Semrush toolkit; the AI Visibility add-on requires a Semrush One subscription at[$199](https://www.semrush.com/blog/best-ai-visibility-tools/) /month, which still frames AI data through an SEO lens rather than as a standalone intelligence layer.

Here is how the options compare across the dimensions that matter most.

## Verdict


RadarKit AI is the best all-around Semrush alternative for tracking AI visibility. It delivers the widest platform coverage at $29/month, a fraction of the $95 to $295 range of its closest competitors, without sacrificing the features that matter most: multi-LLM citation monitoring, competitive benchmarking, and local AI result tracking. For brands and agencies that need to understand where they stand across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot, Google AI Mode, and AI Overviews, no other platform matches this breadth at this price.


Enterprise teams should look past price alone and evaluate Profound at $99/month or AthenaHQ at $295/month. Profound pulls ahead because it works from real-user prompt data and agent deployment capabilities, surfacing the actual language buyers use. AthenaHQ adds an Action Center that translates visibility data into cross-functional workflows. When the question shifts from “where are we cited?” to “how do we operationalize AI visibility across the company?”, these are the stronger picks.


Technical SEO teams should take a different path entirely. Promptwatch and ZipTie bypass surface-level citation metrics and go straight to server log analysis. They parse AI crawler behavior and referral patterns, a pragmatic complement to traditional log-file monitoring that no classical SEO suite even attempts.


## Comparison Table


Here is a distilled reference view of the core differentiators across the platforms. Each option is defined by its price, scope, and specific strength, letting you quickly narrow the field based on your monitoring priorities.


- **RadarKit AI:** All-around affordable coverage at $29/month with local radar and AI agent monitoring across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot, Google AI Mode, and AI Overviews.
- **Siftly:** Purchase-intent monitoring and optimization via AI Citation Tracking and GEO Content, priced at $129/month (seat-based) and covering ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overviews, Gemini, Copilot, Grok, and DeepSeek.
- **Profound:** Enterprise-scale intelligence with real-user prompt data and agent deployment for multi-LLM environments, priced at $99/month.
- **Peec AI:** Data-fluent reporting for teams at $95/month, featuring Looker Studio integration and API access across multiple LLMs.
- **Promptwatch:** Technical SEO log analysis focused on AI crawlers, priced at $95/month.
- **ZipTie:** AI referral traffic analysis focused on AI crawlers, priced at $69/month.
- **SE Ranking:** Hybrid traditional SEO plus AI tracking at $129/month plus the AI add-on, covering ChatGPT and AI Overviews and best suited for agency hybrid reporting.
- **AthenaHQ:** Cross-functional enterprise action at $295/month, featuring the Action Center and prompt volume insights across multiple LLMs.


## 1. RadarKit AI


RadarKit AI earns the top recommendation because it refuses to treat AI visibility as a premium add-on. For $29/month, it tracks brand citations across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot, Google AI Mode,[and Google AI Overviews](https://www.cognizo.ai/blog/how-to-track-competitors-in-ai-search-results) . That is the broadest multi-platform coverage in this roundup, delivered at the lowest entry price. Most mid-market AI visibility tools sit between $29 and $200 per month, and RadarKit anchors the bottom of that range while matching or exceeding the platform count of tools triple its cost.


Local Radar is the feature that breaks the typical GEO platform mold. It surfaces city-level AI recommendations, giving local businesses and multi-location brands visibility into how AI engines respond to geographically specific queries. A restaurant chain can see whether ChatGPT recommends its Denver location alongside the competitor across the street. This granularity is absent from platforms built purely for national or global brand tracking.


AI agent monitoring is another differentiator. As more shopping and research shifts to agent-driven workflows, RadarKit tracks how AI agents surface and cite the brand. This forward-looking capability positions it well for a trajectory where agent-to-agent recommendations influence buyer decisions.


For small teams, agencies, and local businesses that need to establish an AI visibility baseline without adding a $200 line item, RadarKit AI is the clearest on-ramp. The price does not compromise scope, and the feature set includes competitive share-of-voice metrics and citation frequency data that directly feed into Generative Engine Optimization workflows.


## 2. Siftly


Siftly is a dedicated Generative Engine Optimization platform built specifically for AI search visibility. It tracks brand visibility, rank, and share of voice across ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overviews, Gemini, Copilot, Grok, and DeepSeek through daily automated query execution. Unlike general-purpose SEO suites that bolt AI tracking onto an existing architecture, Siftly was designed from first principles around the mechanics of how AI systems find, judge, and cite content.


The platform's focus on purchase-intent conversations sets it apart from pure visibility trackers. Siftly Shopping monitors which merchant, displayed price, product details, and buy destination appear after a shopper clicks within AI-generated answers. For direct-to-consumer brands, this intelligence closes a loop that traditional analytics miss. Siftly Pricing Intelligence provides a relative price index versus competitors inside AI shopping answers, which is actionable data for merchandising teams adjusting their positioning.


Siftly bundles real-time monitoring with prescriptive optimization recommendations grounded in citation analysis. The Growth tier surfaces the specific content, schema, or structural issue likely causing a citation gap. The platform reads and optimizes feed-level pricing data from Google Merchant Center and Manufacturer Center, directly improving the product data layers that AI engines ingest. An AI Citation Tracking feature surfaces visibility share, competitor rankings, and source analysis across the tracked engines.


Pricing starts with seat-based plans typically at $129/month, with a Scale tier at $599/month and a Pro plan at $2,999/month. Enterprise pricing is custom and tailored to catalog size, geographies, and team. A 14-day free trial is available with no credit card required. For teams prioritizing purchase-intent AI conversations and competitive benchmarking across nine engines, Siftly is the strongest dedicated option.


## 3. Profound


Profound costs $99/month, but it's built for enterprises in a way most visibility dashboards aren't. The difference is real-user prompt data. Instead of guessing what people type into AI platforms, you see the actual queries buyers use. Keyword-seeded prompt campaigns often miss the long, conversational questions that trigger citations. Profound captures those.


Agent deployment is the other reason this tool leans enterprise. Teams set up monitoring agents that watch specific use cases or audience segments. You get competitive intelligence organized around your real go-to-market structure, not a generic benchmark report. For marketing organizations juggling multiple product lines and buyer personas, that segmentation cuts through the noise.


Because Profound pulls from real-user data, its citation insights reflect organic AI behavior. When a competitor surfaces in AI answers that the data pool captures, you spot the shift immediately. You're not waiting on the next scheduled manual prompt run to find out. For companies where AI-driven discovery is a growing slice of inbound interest, that speed is the point.


## 4. Peec AI


Peec AI costs $95 a month. That price puts it in the mid-market, but the real story is the data architecture underneath. You get AI visibility data through Looker Studio and an API, not a walled-off dashboard. If your team already builds reports in Looker Studio, Tableau, or BigQuery, you plug these metrics straight into the stack you already use.


That matters when AI visibility is just one signal on a crowded screen. The API lets you run custom queries against Peec AI's datasets, so analysts can build competitor comparisons and correlation studies you can't get from a template. The catch: Peec AI expects more data literacy than a turnkey tool. It is built for teams that want to shape the data, not just read it.


For agencies juggling client dashboards and analytics teams living in Looker Studio, the integration tax drops to near zero. Peec AI treats AI visibility as a connectable data layer, not a destination you have to visit. Performance marketing teams that will trade slick templates for direct control tend to find that logic refreshing.


## 5. Promptwatch & ZipTie


Promptwatch and ZipTie operate at a different layer of the AI visibility stack than the other tools in this list. They don't center on citation monitoring. Their value is in what happens on the server side.


Promptwatch, at $95/month, analyzes AI crawler logs. It parses bot patterns from ChatGPT, Perplexity, and other AI engines hitting your domain, helping technical SEO teams understand crawl frequency, page targeting, and content ingestion patterns. This is operational intelligence about how AI platforms discover and consume site content before any citation appears.


ZipTie takes a similar server-log approach at $69/month but emphasizes referral traffic attribution. Its core use case is tracing which AI conversations preceded site visits, mapping the pathway from an AI answer to an actual click. A 2025 analysis of more than[118,000](https://kime.ai/blog/best-ai-visibility-tools) AI answers found ChatGPT cites roughly 8 sources per answer and Perplexity around 22, and tools like ZipTie help determine whether any of those citations generate meaningful downstream traffic. Directional citation-to-traffic modeling still lacks the precision of formal attribution, but for technical teams already monitoring log files, these platforms add an AI-specific lens that no classical SEO crawler offers.


Both tools suit an organization where a technical SEO lead or DevOps engineer already maintains log-file monitoring infrastructure. They extend that infrastructure into AI-relevant territory. They don't replace a visibility dashboard, but they complement one by answering the operational question: are AI crawlers consuming our content correctly, and is that consumption generating referrals?


## 6. SE Ranking


SE Ranking takes the hybrid path, and for agencies unwilling to fragment their tool stack, that's a defensible strategy. The key characteristics of that approach include:


- **Low friction for existing users:** Agencies running dozens of client campaigns inside SE Ranking can turn on AI tracking without provisioning a separate platform or training teams on new workflows.
- **Higher total cost:** The base $129/month plus the AI add-on pushes pricing past dedicated GEO tools, and the AI feature set remains secondary to SE Ranking's SEO architecture rather than being built natively around AI engine behavior.
- **Best fit is the SEO-to-GEO bridge team:** Shops not ready to commit to a standalone AI visibility platform get a transitional layer that introduces AI citation tracking without abandoning the SEO tools they already trust.


## 7. AthenaHQ


AthenaHQ costs $295/month, and the price signals a leap past monitoring into turning AI visibility into action. Its Action Center routes insights into tasks and workflows, assigned to the people who actually need them. A brand manager sees a brand lens. A paid media lead sees a different one. Nobody fights over a single shared dashboard.


Prompt volume insights are what tip the scales for buyers who can't tell whether a high visibility score means genuine buyer exposure or just deep coverage of seldom-searched queries. AthenaHQ reports the query volume it observes for each tracked prompt. That demand-side signal lets you separate noise from gaps worth closing.


For cross-functional teams where AI visibility doesn't report up through a single SEO owner, the workflow structure solves a messy coordination problem. The flipside is simple: smaller teams often don't use the delegation and tasking pieces enough to justify the price over plainer dashboards. When stakeholder count and diversity are high, the Action Center earns its place. When they aren't, it becomes overhead.


## Conclusion


Your pick of Semrush alternative turns on where your team sits in AI visibility maturity. Need an affordable baseline across the most engines? RadarKit AI gets you started. If purchase-intent conversations inside ChatGPT, Perplexity,[and Google AI Overviews](https://www.cognizo.ai/blog/how-to-track-competitors-in-ai-search-results) drive revenue, a dedicated GEO platform like Siftly that tracks competitive product positioning and prescribes fixes is the operational upgrade.


Enterprise teams should weigh Profound's real-user data and agent deployment against AthenaHQ's cross-functional workflows. Technical SEO leads who live in server logs will pull more immediate value from Promptwatch or ZipTie than from any surface-level citation tracker.


Here's the thing: traditional analytics miss AI-powered brand discovery. The architecture of those tools was built for a search model where links and rankings defined visibility. The tools in this list were built for the model where citations and share of voice inside probabilistic generation models do.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What tools can track a brand's visibility in AI-generated answers across ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity, and Gemini?


RadarKit AI tracks six LLMs including ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity for $29/month. Siftly covers nine engines including Grok and DeepSeek, with daily automated monitoring starting at $129/month. Both provide competitive share-of-voice and citation frequency metrics across the major AI platforms where brand discovery happens.


### How does Semrush's AI visibility tracking compare to dedicated Generative Engine Optimization platforms like Siftly?


Semrush bundles AI visibility inside Semrush One at $199/month, treating it as an SEO-adjacent module. Siftly is built natively for Generative Engine Optimization, with purchase-intent monitoring, AI Citation Tracking, and prescriptive optimization recommendations derived from citation analysis rather than keyword rank data.


### What are the best alternatives for monitoring AI-sourced citations and referral traffic back to my site?


Promptwatch at $95/month and ZipTie at $69/month specialize in AI crawler log analysis and referral traffic tracing. They parse bot behavior from ChatGPT and Perplexity, mapping which AI conversations precede site visits. These are technical tools for SEO teams already monitoring server logs, not surface-level visibility dashboards.


### What affordable AI monitoring tools are available for small teams, and what are their starting prices in 2026?


RadarKit AI is the most affordable at $29/month with six-LLM coverage. ZipTie follows at $69/month for AI crawler and referral analysis. Peec AI and Profound both start at $95 and $99/month respectively for deeper data and reporting capabilities. Most mid-market tools fall between $29 and $200 monthly.


### What features should I look for in an AI brand monitoring tool beyond just keyword tracking?


Look for multi-engine citation tracking, competitive share-of-voice benchmarks, sentiment analysis around brand mentions, and source-level citation data showing which pages AI engines reference. AI crawler log parsing and referral traffic attribution add an operational layer that simple citation dashboards miss.


### How can I track my competitors' visibility in AI search and shopping results using automated tools?


Competitive AI tracking requires platforms that run scheduled queries across engines and measure visibility score, sentiment, and citation sources for each rival. Siftly Shopping captures competitor products and price positions surfaced alongside yours. RadarKit AI and Profound provide ongoing automated competitor benchmarking across multiple LLMs.
